landManager: Deschutes and Willamette National Forests (Diamond Peak Wilderness)
Mt. Hood National Forest (Mount Hood Wilderness above the ski area)
storedPass: Oregon Sno-Park permit, November 1 to April 30

landManager: Deschutes National Forest (Bend-Fort Rock and Sisters Ranger Districts) - Three Sisters Wilderness
storedPass: Yes at both trailheads - Northwest Forest Pass, an interagency pass, or $5 day pass per vehicle

landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, Methow Valley Ranger District; Lake Chelan-Sawtooth Wilderness
drive: From Twisp, drive Twisp River Road west approximately 22-24 miles to the Scatter Creek/Scatter Lake trailhead (~3,100-3,200 ft), about 50 yards past the Slate Creek Trail junction sign.
From Interstate 90 exit 52, turn onto State Route 906, then continue onto Erste Strasse (Alpental Access Road) and follow it for 1.1 miles to a left turn into the lot just below the main lodges.

landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass likely required at developed trailheads (e.g. Alpine Lookout via FR 6910) — $5/day or $30/year.
drive: From Leavenworth, drive US Highway 2 west approximately 17.4-17.7 miles (or from Stevens Pass, drive east about 18 miles) to just past the Nason Creek Rest Area.

names: US-2 roadside pullout (Nason Creek, ~6.5 miles east of Stevens Pass)
landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest
storedPass: None required — unofficial roadside scramble with no maintained trailhead
drive: From the unofficial US-2 pullout near the WSDOT yard ~6.5 miles east of Stevens Pass: cross the highway and the BNSF rail line after the Nason Creek bridge

landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest (Methow Valley Ranger District)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass required at the Rattlesnake (West Fork Methow) Trailhead — $5/day or $30/annual (America the Beautiful pass also honored).

names: FR 6835 pullout past the East Fork Foss bridge
landManager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Skykomish Ranger District)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass ($30/yr) or America the Beautiful pass, or a $5/day pass at developed trailheads.
drive: From the FR 6835 pullout past the East Fork Foss bridge

landManager: Olympic National Forest, Hood Canal Ranger District (Buckhorn Wilderness); the summit sits on the boundary with Olympic National Park.
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass ($5/day or $30/annual)
drive: From Sequim, drive US-101 south about 5 miles to Louella Road, follow it 0.9 mile and turn left onto Palo Alto Road, then go nearly 6 miles and keep right onto FR-28. Turn right onto FR-2880 for 1.7 miles, left onto FR-2870 for 2.6 miles, right onto FR-2860 for 4.9 miles, then slight right onto FR-270 for 1.6 miles to the parking area.

landManager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Mt. Baker Ranger District)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass required at most trailheads — $30/year or $5/day.
drive: From the FS-3160 road-end parking (via Canyon Creek Road FS-31)

names: FR 4096 Pullout / Merry Brook Climbers' Path
landManager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Darrington Ranger District)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass required at Mountain Loop Highway trailheads — $5/day or $30/year.

landManager: National Park Service — North Cascades National Park (Stephen Mather Wilderness)
drive: From the end of Bacon Creek Road

landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, Wenatchee River Ranger District (Alpine Lakes Wilderness)
Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Darrington Ranger District)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass required at Mountain Loop Highway trailheads — $5/day or $30/year.
drive: Begins from the Big Four viewpoint / Ice Caves Trailhead on the Mountain Loop Highway, as with the peak's other technical routes.

names: Big Four Picnic Area / Ice Caves Trailhead
landManager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Darrington Ranger District)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass required at Mountain Loop Highway trailheads — $5/day or $30/year.
drive: Take the Mountain Loop Highway east from Granite Falls, pass the Verlot Ranger Station after about 10 miles, and continue about 14 miles to the signed turn for the Big Four picnic area on the right.

landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest — Pasayten Wilderness
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass required at trailheads (e.g. Andrews Creek, Chewuch River) — $5/day or $30/annual.

landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest — Pasayten Wilderness
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass required at trailheads (e.g. Andrews Creek, Chewuch River) — $5/day or $30/annual.
drive: From Mazama, head north on Lost River Road and after about 9 miles turn right onto FR-5400. Climb about 8.7 miles to Harts Pass; the road is narrow and rugged, suited to high-clearance vehicles only, and is typically open July through September.

names: "Rainy Pass Picnic Area / Lake Ann Trailhead (SR-20)"
landManager: National Park Service — North Cascades National Park (Stephen Mather Wilderness)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass ($5 day / $30 annual) or Interagency Pass
drive: From Marblemount, drive SR-20 east about 50 miles to Rainy Pass; the picnic area and Lake Ann trailhead lot is on the south side of the highway.

landManager: USDA Forest Service, Olympic National Forest — Hood Canal Ranger District, Quilcene Office, 295142 Highway 101 S, Quilcene, WA 98376, (360) 765-2200 (open Tue–Wed, 9am–3pm).
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass

names: PCT Southbound Trailhead at Stevens Pass
landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest (Alpine Lakes Wilderness)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass or America the Beautiful pass

landManager: Trailhead is on Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Skykomish Ranger District); Chain/Doelle Lakes and Bulls Tooth itself sit across the Cascade crest in the Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest's Alpine Lakes Wilderness (Wenatchee River Ranger District, Icicle Creek drainage).
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass ($30/yr) or America the Beautiful pass, or a $5/day pass at developed trailheads.
drive: Start at the Stevens Pass PCT-South trailhead (large lot on the south side of US 2, ~4,060 ft, just east of the ski area buildings).

landManager: Mount Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest, Snoqualmie Ranger District; Alpine Lakes Wilderness
drive: Same access as the peak's other routes: via the Dutch Miller Gap Trailhead at the Dingford Creek gate on the Middle Fork Snoqualmie Road, then about 7.7 miles of closed road east up the valley on foot or by bike

landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest — Alpine Lakes Wilderness
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass required at Stuart Lake, Eightmile, and Snow Lakes trailheads — $5/day or $30/annual (overnight permit holders get a covering parking pass instead).
drive: From Highway 2 on the west side of Leavenworth, turn south onto Icicle Road and drive 8.4 miles, then turn left onto Forest Road 7601 (Eightmile Road, washboard and potholed) and go 3.1 miles to the Eightmile trailhead parking.

names: Pinnacle Peak Trailhead (Reflection Lakes, Stevens Canyon Road)
landManager: National Park Service — Mount Rainier National Park
storedPass: Standard Mount Rainier NP entrance fee: $30/vehicle (7 days), $55 Mount Rainier annual pass, or $80 America the Beautiful interagency annual pass.
drive: From the Nisqually entrance of Mount Rainier National Park, drive Paradise Road about 15 miles to the Stevens Canyon Road junction, turn right and go 1.5 miles to the Reflection Lakes parking area; the trailhead is on the south side of the road.

landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, Cle Elum Ranger District (Alpine Lakes Wilderness).
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass ($30/yr) or America the Beautiful pass, or a $5/day pass at developed trailheads.
drive: From Roslyn, follow SR 903 north about 14.8 miles to the end of the maintained road, bear right onto Forest Road 4330, and continue on gravel to the trailhead at its end.

landManager: Washington Department of Fish and Wildlife — Chelan Butte Wildlife Area (state land, not USFS or BLM)
storedPass: Discover Pass (Washington state parking pass) required, not a Northwest Forest Pass.
drive: From the town of Chelan, take SR 150 (E Woodin Rd), then Sanders St, Farnham St, S. Saunders St, and E. Iowa Ave to the WDFW Chelan Butte trailhead parking lot, and climb the Chelan Butte Trail directly toward the summit.

landManager: National Park Service — Olympic National Park (Olympic Wilderness)
storedPass: Olympic NP entrance fee: $30/vehicle (7-day), $55 annual Olympic NP pass, or $80 America the Beautiful interagency annual pass.
drive: From US-101 about a mile south of Amanda Park, turn east onto South Shore Road and follow it 7.7 paved miles and 4.9 gravel miles to the junction at the Quinault River bridge, then continue right about 6 more gravel miles to the road-end trailhead.

landManager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Mt. Baker Ranger District) — Mount Baker Wilderness, with some upper routes crossing into North Cascades National Park
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass required at most trailheads — $30/year or $5/day.
drive: From Acme on WA-9, turn east onto Mosquito Lake Road and follow it about 9 miles, cross the Middle Fork Nooksack River and continue onto Forest Road 38 for about 11 miles to the Elbow Lake trailhead. Since July 2026 Forest Road 38 has been closed to vehicles by a washout at milepost 7.
